headline: High: shared browser/MCP-enabled collaboration creates prompt-injection, leakage, and action-conflict risks; TREK’s real-time collaborative defaults amplify cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: kotaemon ingests documents/HTML/MHTML and TREK runs a real-time collaborative AI with browsers and MCP. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content from one can be treated as instructions by the other. The interaction is inferred from docs only, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF TREK exposes browser-rendered or MCP-fed content to kotaemon without provenance tagging, injection is reachable.
IF either agent parses the other’s output as instructions rather than data, the attack path exists.
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following on imported content.
Add provenance labels to all cross-agent content.
Restrict MCP tools to read-only for shared sessions.
Use a manual review step before executing any extracted instructions.
requires-engineering: isolate the agents onto separate workspaces.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents handle sensitive secrets and documents, and both have file surfaces plus network egress. kotaemon can send content to external LLM APIs, while TREK stores travel.db/uploads/logs and uses MCP/OIDC. In a shared deployment, sensitive documents or secrets can cross from one agent into the other and then out to third parties.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace or upload directory, leakage becomes direct.
IF kotaemon forwards imported files to external APIs, sensitive data can leave the boundary.
IF TREK ingests shared documents or uploads, those contents can be exposed in logs or collaborative views.
mitigations: Separate storage directories for each agent.
Remove secrets from shared documents before ingestion.
Turn off external API calls for sensitive sessions.
Review TREK logs for accidental secret capture.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls and DLP.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: kotaemon supports multiple instances and broad egress; TREK is real-time collaborative with multiple instances and MCP. Both can mutate shared resources if deployed together, but the profiles do not prove a shared writable directory or git state. Uncertainty therefore keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path, write conflicts are reachable.
IF both are granted overlapping OAuth or API scopes on the same backend, mutable-resource conflicts occur.
IF an orchestrator lacks locking, concurrent edits can overwrite each other.
mitigations: Assign separate storage paths.
Limit each agent to distinct API credentials.
Pause one agent during critical writes.
Add file-locking or optimistic concurrency checks.
requires-engineering: introduce a coordinator for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is described as a real-time collaborative travel planner with AI built in, so it can plausibly act on upstream outputs. kotaemon produces document-derived answers and citations. If TREK consumes kotaemon output without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into bookings, plans, or user-facing decisions; the docs-only evidence warrants the higher severity.
conditions: IF TREK uses kotaemon output as authoritative input, cascading error is active.
IF either agent auto-generates user-facing actions from the other’s text, downstream mistakes propagate.
IF no human verification step exists between them, the chain remains unbroken.
mitigations: Require human approval before actions.
Show source citations alongside every imported answer.
Add a verification prompt before TREK acts on kotaemon output.
Limit kotaemon to retrieval-only mode for shared workflows.
requires-engineering: add structured schemas and validation.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents touch regulated-looking personal data, but the profiles do not prove a specific residency or certification mismatch. The clearest issue is retention/logging: TREK explicitly stores logs and travel.db, while kotaemon handles chat transcripts and documents. That creates a plausible policy mismatch on the same data class, but not enough for high severity.
conditions: IF the same personal data is stored in TREK logs and kotaemon transcripts, retention mismatch exists.
IF EU PII is routed through a US-only backend not shown in the profiles, compliance risk increases.
IF deletion requests must propagate across both systems and do not, subject-rights handling fails.
mitigations: Minimize logged personal data.
Set short retention on TREK logs.
Avoid storing sensitive chat transcripts in kotaemon.
Document data-flow ownership for each class.
requires-engineering: align residency and deletion workflows.
